title: Which Gol de Ozil? The 2016 Champions League Goal and an AI Video Guide
metaTitle: Gol de Ozil: The Classic 2016 Goal and AI Video Guide | Ozil Goal
description: Identify the match, score and 88th-minute winner behind gol de ozil, distinguish the original goal from the bounce shot and AI versions, and make a football clip from your own photo.
label: The Story of Gol de Ozil
excerpt: Start with Ludogorets versus Arsenal in the Champions League, explore the story of Özil’s late winner and learn how to make an AI football video from a personal photo.
intro: **Gol de ozil** simply means “Özil’s goal” in Spanish; it does not inherently identify a particular match. If the clip shows him lifting the ball over the goalkeeper, evading defenders and finishing calmly, this article covers Mesut Özil’s 2016 Champions League winner against Ludogorets. Understanding the real match also helps explain the AI football versions made from photographs.

sections.title: Start with the date, opponent and score

blocks.text: The match took place on 1 November 2016, on Matchday 4 in Champions League Group A. Arsenal visited Ludogorets at the Vasil Levski National Stadium in Sofia, Bulgaria. The final score was 2–3, with Özil scoring the winner in the 88th minute. You can verify these details in [UEFA’s official match statistics](https://www.uefa.com/newsfiles/UCL/2017/2019330_TS.pdf).
Adding “Ludogorets 2016” to your search makes this goal easier to find. Searching only for the player’s name and “goal” may also return clips from his other clubs and matches.

sections.title: Why was it a late winner?

blocks.text: The hosts scored in the 12th and 15th minutes, leaving Arsenal 0–2 down. Xhaka pulled one back in the 20th minute and Giroud equalised in the 42nd. Özil’s strike broke a 2–2 deadlock and ultimately turned a draw into an away win. The scoring timeline appears in the same [UEFA match statistics](https://www.uefa.com/newsfiles/UCL/2017/2019330_TS.pdf).

The victory also helped Arsenal reach the Champions League round of 16 for the 17th consecutive season. The comeback and qualification context give the moment emotional weight beyond the quality of the dribbling. See [UEFA’s match report](https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0233-0e9591456f5d-b1a200c579f0-1000--ozil-completes-arsenal-comeback-at-ludogorets/).

sections.title: Watch the sequence in three parts

blocks.text: Özil finished the move after a pass from Elneny. [TyC Sports’ retrospective](https://www.tycsports.com/curiosidades/la-historia-detras-del-golazo-de-oezil-que-ahora-hacen-shrek-woody-y-otros-id766686.html) describes him lifting the ball over the goalkeeper, sending two defenders the wrong way and then finishing calmly.

items: First, watch how he deals with the goalkeeper: lifting the ball changes its height and the route needed to chase it.
Then watch the pause in front of goal: he observes the defenders’ movement before choosing his next touch.
Finally, watch the finish: the most striking work has already happened in the preceding touches, leaving a simple final action.

blocks.text: This is a useful order for studying the real sequence, not a promise about every frame of the fixed AI template. For more match context, continue with [the story of Özil’s goal against Ludogorets](/mesut-ozil-ludogorets-goal).

sections.title: Two common mix-ups: the match and the shot name

blocks.text: First, this was not the first meeting on 19 October 2016. Arsenal won that home match 6–0 and Özil scored a hat-trick; this article covers the 3–2 away win two weeks later. The opponent was the same, but the date, score and goals were different. Compare [UEFA’s report of the earlier match](https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0232-0e9546f03574-b7f950806233-1000/).

Second, the Ozil bounce or chop shot is a separate finishing topic. Arsenal released an [official video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5aJcOd4sL38) in which Özil explains that technique. Do not treat that name as a synonym for his solo winning goal against Ludogorets.

sections.title: Make an AI football video from your own photo

blocks.text: If you want a football scene starring you, you can use the [Ozil Goal generator](/#generator). The site uses a fixed template with no custom action or prompt field. The result is a creative work, not footage of the original match.

items: Prepare one clear photo of a single adult whose image you have permission to use. JPG, PNG and WebP are supported, with a maximum file size of 10MB.
Upload the photo and check the person and generation details. Each generation costs {ozilCredits} credits.
Generate a 15-second vertical 9:16 video with sound. See the [template guide](/ozil-goal-generator/ozil-goal-ai-template) for the input and output requirements.
Preview the entire clip to check the face, the ball’s position and the continuity of the movement before choosing a version to share.

sections.title: Keep the match and your creation clear when sharing

blocks.text: Label the post as an “AI-generated football clip” and use the platform’s AI label where available. When discussing the original goal, link to the match source; when showing your own work, explain that it was created from a photo. This preserves the fun of the football scene without suggesting that you actually played in that match.

faqs.question: Did Özil score this gol de ozil while playing for Real Madrid?
faqs.answer: No. The goal discussed here was scored on 1 November 2016, when he represented Arsenal against Ludogorets.

faqs.question: Was the 88th-minute winner scored in stoppage time?
faqs.answer: It was a late winning goal, but the 88th minute is still within the regulation 90 minutes. It should not be described as a stoppage-time goal.

faqs.question: Do I need to write a prompt or upload the original footage?
faqs.answer: No. This site needs only one eligible photo of an adult whose image you have permission to use. It generates from a fixed template and has no custom prompt field.
